title: Eric the Eel at the Olympics
subtitle: 考点：体育精神 / compete, cheer, set a record
passage: At the Sydney Olympics in 2000, a young swimmer from Equatorial Guinea became famous around the world. His name was Eric Moussambani. He had learned to swim only a few months before, and he had never seen an Olympic-size pool.

In his race, the other two swimmers made false starts, so Eric swam alone. He was very tired in the last part, and the crowd stood up and cheered for him. He finished the race much more slowly than the other Olympic swimmers, but he was proud. 'I just wanted to finish,' he said. Eric did not win a medal, but he showed the real spirit of the Games. He later became a coach and helped to train young swimmers in his country.
